decisions.reason: The Webster County/Iowa DNR Des Moines River trail materials identify Lehigh as a named water-trail access. Existing source notes already classify this as a practical area anchor rather than a surveyed ramp point. No defensible replacement water-edge coordinate was found, so preserve the anchor and require an on-site ramp check.

decisions.site: Riverside Park / Milwaukee Rotary Centennial Arboretum landing
decisions.reason: Milwaukee County designates Riverside Park as an East Bank launch near the Urban Ecology Center. UEC directs visitors from its parking lot along a path to the canoe launch. The current point is retained and relabeled as a park-access anchor; it is not the water-edge point.

American Whitewater and How's Your River describe Shotgun as a rapid to scout or portage from river left. The route source itself says this is not a public landing. Removed it from the access list while retaining the scouting/portage safety instructions.

decisions.site: Canalside Buffalo Commercial Slip / public low dock
decisions.reason: The Buffalo waterfront manager publishes current docking instructions; the City's waterfront plan documents a lower dock intended for kayak use. Keep the coordinate as a dock/site anchor and retain the existing event, authorization, traffic, and water-entry caveats. No better current launch-edge coordinate was documented.

The prior coordinate is the Forest Service recreation/campground facility point. The Forest Service Eleven Point river map separately publishes the Greer Crossing river-access point as 36°47′36.38″N, 91°19′53.82″W; current Forest Service destination material confirms that Greer Crossing has a boat ramp and day-use area. The mapped point is an access anchor, not a surveyed ramp edge.

decisions.site: Monkton Road / Monkton Station Gunpowder access
decisions.reason: Maryland DNR identifies Monkton Station as a public park facility and documents its limited parking; American Whitewater names Monkton Road as the access in this Gunpowder reach. Neither source isolates a water-edge launch coordinate. Keep the existing access-area anchor and its carry/parking warnings.

Chickasaw County's park listing identifies Pearl Rock as a canoe launch on the Cedar River and gives the 1072 305th Street location; the City of Nashua lists it in its Cedar River access chain. The available manager sources do not publish a separate surveyed water-edge point, so retain the existing anchor and limited-parking caveat.

decisions.site: Fisherman's Park / Burt Dam below-dam access area
decisions.reason: The Town of Newfane waterfront plan describes Fisherman's Park as town-owned fishing access with parking and a steep site. It does not establish a canoe/kayak launch or legal loaded-boat carry. Relabeled the point and kept the route withheld pending Town confirmation of watercraft use and a safe water entry below Burt Dam.

decisions.site: Princeton Jefferson Street / Hiestand Park Landing
decisions.reason: The City of Princeton identifies a 2018 kayak launch and boat pier in Hiestand Park. The published city material confirms the public launch site but does not isolate the water-side edge, so keep the existing park/launch-area anchor.

The selected Sheboygan River route source describes Highway C as a bridge/corridor reference and explicitly says it is not a fully confirmed primary landing. Removed the intermediate access marker; the route still starts at Dassow Park and ends at the verified River Park canoe ramp, and the narrative continues to caution against relying on the bridge as a bailout.
